sources.citation: Sumbuk, Kenneth Memson. 1999. Morphosyntax of Sare. PhD thesis, University of Waikato. xiii+335 pp. (hdl 10289/13888). Ch.1 with Chart 1.1 'The position of Sare within the Sepik area Papuan languages (Laycock 1973)'; 2.2.1 Stress (pp.40-42) for Sare/Kapriman only.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Read held by the project: the thesis describes Sare (Kapriman, kapr1245) only; p.2 'Of the Sepik Hill Family, to which Sare belongs, only Alamblak (Bruce 1984), has a comprehensive description'; the explicit stress rule (2.2.1, pp.40-42: secondary stress initial, primary stress final in disyllables and penultimate in longer words) is for Sare alone; nothing on this language.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert & Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-36. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing on Kalou. The only stress remark in the paper (p. 10) is 'Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak' - Left May (Arai) languages, another family; tone mentions concern Upper Sepik/May River languages.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In Stephen A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 731-766. Canberra: Australian National University. DOI 10.15144/PL-C38.731.
sources.note: No Kalou-specific phonology. Sec. 2.11.1 (p. 732) lists features 'widespread throughout the phylum, and.. found in a majority of the languages which comprise it', including 'low number of vowel phonemes', 'occurrence of a schwa-phoneme which is only quasi-phonemic', and 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems'; no statement on stress placement anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). The Tama Stock section (2.11.3.1.2.2, pp. 746-748) gives phonemes, pronouns and verb morphology for Mehek and Mayo only.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry no. 80 'KALOU', p. 23 (p. 27).
sources.note: Nothing. The Kalou entry gives only villages (Yawa, Yilui), the test wordlist DCL70 (Pagaray/Yilui) and the note 'mentioned in Laycock (1968:62), but there unnamed'. The book's general Sepik-Ramu phonology remarks (p. 20) concern vowel inventories and consonant series; a full-text search for stress/accent the whole text finds no stress/accent statement for any language.
